subject: Pricing guardrail / trigger adjustment request
messages:

Subject: Revised pricing exhibit + protection clause

Stephanie — attaching our redline to the Pricing Exhibit. Two high-level asks: 1) narrow the floor so we aren’t locked into the current minimum once usage grows; 2) add a ‘Customer Protection Trigger’ that pauses automatic true-up increases if usage drops below a sustained baseline for >60 days.

We circled the clauses in the PDF (SB-Redline_Pricing_Exhibit_v3.pdf).

Can your team review and confirm whether these are deal-breakers or if we can propose alternate language? We need this resolved before procurement completes internal approvals next week.

Stonebridge Analytics

From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

Date: 2026-11-15T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Revised pricing exhibit + protection clause

Looping you both in — Stonebridge sent a marked-up Pricing Exhibit asking to narrow the minimum commitment (floor) and add a 60-day Customer Protection Trigger that would pause automatic true-ups/step increases if usage drops. They say procurement needs clarity by EOW.

Notes / ask:
- Karthik: can legal propose defensible language that preserves our predictable revenue while addressing their concern about transient dips?
- Marcus: what's the commercial downside if we accept a 60-day trigger with conditional restart? Any compromise on ramp bands or minimums we should push?

I suggest we propose a middle path: shorter pause window (45 days), a one-time restart fee to discourage gaming, and caps on cumulative discount to preserve lifetime value. Happy to draft a counter if you confirm approach.

—Stephanie
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-16T08:34:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Revised pricing exhibit + protection clause

Stephanie / Marcus — reviewed the SB redline. High-level legal positions:

1) Floor narrowing: we can agree to a seasonal adjustment clause but must tie it to objective metrics (30-day rolling average) and limit carve-outs to once-per-annual period. Absolute removal of a floor is high risk to revenue predictability and will require commercial makegood.

2) Customer Protection Trigger: acceptable if (a) it’s a temporary suspension (not termination) of step increases, (b) trigger defined by two consecutive 30-day periods below baseline (i.e., 60 days) or alternately two non-consecutive months within a 90-day lookback, and (c) automatic restart occurs when usage returns to baseline or higher for 30 consecutive days.

3) Safeguards we must add: anti-abuse language (no gaming via split accounts), a restart administrative fee ($10k or prorated monthly minimum), and a cap on cumulative concessions (e.g., protection can apply up to two times in the contract term).

I drafted sample clause language in the attached doc (placed in Drive link). If commercial accepts the restart fee and the two-time cap, legal can live with the protection trigger.

—Karthik
Head of Legal (Commercial) | Redwood Inference
From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-16T11:12:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Revised pricing exhibit + protection clause

Thanks — commercial view:

- Revenue impact: if we accept a 60-day pause without constraints it could reduce realized ARR in year 1 by ~8–12% for this deal profile. A $10k restart fee seems low; recommend $25k or a one-month minimum invoice instead (whichever is higher).
- Compromise: agree to 45-day sustained drop OR two non-consecutive months within 90 days to trigger pause; apply restart as one-month minimum invoice plus administrative fee $15k. Limit protection to 2 occurrences per 12 months, and require a 30-day lookback for restart condition.
- Floors: propose a dynamic floor tied to the prior quarter, with a fall-back minimum equal to 60% of Year 1 committed spend (so they can’t drop below a meaningful band).

If legal signs off on the higher restart fee/one-month minimum, I’ll take this to pricing and we’ll prepare a clean counter to send to Stonebridge.

Marcus Lin
VP, Revenue | Redwood Inference
From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
To: emartens@stonebridge.ai, contracts@stonebridge.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-18T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Revised pricing exhibit + protection clause — Redwood counter proposal

Elena — thanks for the redline and for surfacing the protection concern. We want to keep predictable economics for both sides, so attached is a proposed counter that aims to bridge both parties. Key points: 

1) Protection Trigger — counter: protection may pause automatic step increases when usage is below the baseline for either (a) 45 consecutive days, or (b) two non-consecutive months within a 90-day period. The suspension is temporary and will automatically end when usage meets the restart threshold for 30 consecutive days.

2) Restart / Safeguard — counter includes a one-month minimum invoice or $15,000 administrative fee (whichever is higher) to restart step increases; protection can be invoked a maximum of two times per 12-month period. Anti-abuse clause added to prevent account splitting.

3) Floors — instead of eliminating the minimum we propose a dynamic floor set to 60% of the prior quarter’s committed spend with a hard minimum floor equal to 60% of Year 1 committed value.

We’ve attached a clean exhibit with tracked changes accepted and the order form with markups: SB-Redline_Pricing_Exhibit_v3.pdf and OrderForm_SB_Markups.docx. Please let us know if this lands for you — if Stonebridge can accept the restart mechanics we should be able to move to signature next week.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
